_comment: CORPUS PROBE PACKAGES. Host-shaped packages chosen to intersect the
synthetic advisory corpus in this directory: openssl 3.1.3-r0 (apk) and
busybox 1.36.1-r16 (apk) against the Alpine secdb fixture, and
python3-requests 2.25.1-3.el9 (rpm) sitting exactly ON the Red Hat CSAF
fixture's fixed version so the backport false-positive class is asserted.
The deb openssl row is SEAM 1's probe: it cannot be consulted at all.
THIS FILE IS NOT A RECORDING OF internal/collector/host AND IS NEVER
EVIDENCE ABOUT IT. It used to be called host-packages.json and it used to
stand in for host.Collect's output; the harness's own tripwire fired on CI
the moment a real package manager appeared, because a hand-written file is
the worst available evidence for a collector that can be run. The chain now
runs host.Collect wherever a package manager exists and cites THAT for the
host-inventory link. See hostInventoryForChain.
What a real inventory cannot do is intersect a synthetic corpus: no machine
has openssl 3.1.3-r0 with CVE-2026-1001 against it, and none ever will. So
these four rows stay, under a name that says what they are, and the
comparator and emitter links are proven over them on every host.
The keys are host.Package's JSON tags (ecosystem/package/version/arch), so
a change to that struct breaks this file rather than silently ignoring it.
NOTE WHAT IS MISSING: there is no purl field, because host.Package has no
purl field. That is not an omission in this fixture; it is the seam the
harness reports.
